name: Jade Cole
life: “I still remember watching a family photograph being taken from another window.” People around the approach to Seabright Court know Jade by a small Thursday habit. Jade likes to watch the beach traffic thin enough for workers going the other way.
voice: I am the parent staying away. I booked a room facing the beach because staying away is harder than I admitted.
appearance: Jade has a thin scattering of white hair over the crown, a long face and high cheekbones, and a favorite piece of clothing, a pale blue work shirt. It usually goes with a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light. When somebody else has the floor, Jade holds eye contact until the other person has finished.
personality: Jade talks very little about private fear and recognizes it quickly in strangers. Offering a choice of seats is one of Jade's ways of saying that it is all right to leave.
agenda: To decide whether to come down from the hotel room.
family: Bess Kaur is Jade’s cousin. Jade chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Bess brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *One clean day*, Bess says, “I had to leave early for watch. Somebody packed the sheet cake in ten little boxes so I could keep talking about it.”
connections: Owen Green. The old friend's speech will sound quite different if the reluctant parent comes down to listen.

reactions.response: Jade asks the couple if they want to begin under fog or wait, without extending the celebration for a photograph.

reactions.response: Jade says only what happened and lets the absent person keep their reasons.
